requirements.title: ICHAR argument restrictions
requirements.definition: C shall be a representable character value of length one, and KIND shall be a scalar integer constant expression.

pending.ICHAR-C-character-length-one-representab: Use default one-character values drawn from the required character set; mutate C to length two and to a noncharacter expression as source-control restrictions with no diagnostic facet.
pending.ICHAR-KIND-scalar-integer-constant-expre: Use absent KIND and a selected integer kind constant; mutate KIND to a nonconstant variable as a source-control restriction with no diagnostic facet.

requirements.title: ICHAR result is integer with selected or default kind
requirements.definition: The ICHAR result is integer; with KIND present its kind is the specified integer kind, and with KIND absent its kind is default integer.

pending.ICHAR-result-integer-kind-from-KIND: Use a selected integer kind constant capable of representing small required-character positions; assert KIND(ICHAR('A',KIND=ik)) equals ik without asserting a fixed code.
pending.ICHAR-result-default-integer-kind-withou: Call ICHAR on a required one-character default value with absent KIND and assert KIND(result) equals KIND(0).

requirements.title: ICHAR positions include CHAR inverse witnesses and processor-dependent native positions
requirements.definition: The result returned for C is the position of C in the processor collating sequence associated with C's kind. For default characters constructed by CHAR at guaranteed in-range positions, the CHAR/ICHAR inverse fixes those selected numeric positions; arbitrary representable default characters still have processor-dependent absolute positions.

pending.ICHAR-CHAR-index-round-trip-guaranteed-r: Use default character kind indices 0, 32, and 65; clauses 6.1 and 7.4.4.2 guarantee more than 65 default characters from the required letters, digits, blank, underscore, and special characters, so each index is in 0..n-1. Assert ICHAR(CHAR(i)) == i for each selected i, with a mutation changing one index or replacing CHAR by a literal control.
pending.ICHAR-arbitrary-character-position-proce: No portable oracle fixes the absolute native numeric position for an arbitrary representable character such as default 'X' on a non-ASCII processor; plans for such characters use nonnegative range samples and order/equality consistency only.

requirements.title: ICHAR result range and capacity obligations
requirements.definition: The ICHAR result is nonnegative and less than the number of characters in the relevant collating sequence, and the result kind shall be capable of representing that number.

pending.ICHAR-result-nonnegative: Use several required one-character default values including blank, digit, and letter; assert each ICHAR result is greater than or equal to zero.
pending.ICHAR-result-less-than-collating-sequenc: No portable oracle exposes the processor's collating-sequence size n for each kind; a future documented character-profile record is needed before checking the upper bound.
pending.ICHAR-result-kind-represents-sequence-si: No portable oracle proves that an arbitrary requested integer kind represents the processor's complete character-set size n without an independent profile of n and supported integer ranges.

requirements.title: ICHAR ordering and equality are consistent with character comparison
requirements.definition: For representable characters C and D, C <= D is true exactly together with ICHAR(C) <= ICHAR(D), and C == D is true exactly together with ICHAR(C) == ICHAR(D).

pending.ICHAR-order-consistent-with-character-le: Use pairs of required default characters whose character <= results are checked directly, including equal and unequal pairs; assert the ICHAR integer comparison has the same logical value.
pending.ICHAR-equality-consistent-with-character: Use equal and distinct one-character required values; assert character equality and ICHAR equality agree while avoiding any fixed numeric code.

accounting.rationale: Description defines the purpose of the ICHAR intrinsic.
Classifies ICHAR as a elemental function; general class semantics are owned by the intrinsic framework.
Result Value paragraph is split into processor-dependent absolute position, range/capacity obligations, and portable order/equality consistency.
Absolute native positions are controlled by the processor collating sequence rather than a fixed standard code.
Example is conditional on an ASCII collating sequence and does not require default ASCII.

Every unit hash-verified by an independent reviewer across two rounds; bit results are observed in bit context, IBITS reaches its high-bit edge, and ICHAR(CHAR(i)) == i is planned for positions the default character set is guaranteed to contain. Source accounting only.
